BURSEVI:v10p88/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p88/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p88/r4.claim: They barred the poor from the garden; a miskīn has nothing and is more destitute than a faqīr. Forbidding entry emphatically forbids permitting it.

BURSEVI:v10p88/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p88/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p88/r5.claim: Ḥard means forceful prevention with anger; they thought themselves able to deny the poor their share, but only achieved deprivation.

BURSEVI:v10p88/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p88/r6.speaker: الكشاف
BURSEVI:v10p88/r6.claim: Al-Kashshāf says they intended to distress the poor despite their ability to benefit them, but instead lost their wealth and suffered deprivation.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p433/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p433/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p433/r5.claim: The whispered prohibition against a needy person entering repeats the parable’s portrayal of the owners’ stinginess already signaled in verse 18.

QUSHAYRI:v3p344/r3.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p344/r3.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p344/r3.claim: On ḥard can mean that they thought themselves able to carry out the plan, or that they were angry with the poor.

FARRA:v3p174/r6.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p174/r6.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p174/r6.claim: The justest brother's call to tasbih means to make an exception by saying إن شاء الله, as in the instruction to remember God after forgetting.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p242/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p242/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p242/r11.claim: They whispered so the poor would not hear them; their secret plan was to keep anyone poor from entering the garden.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p242/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p242/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p242/r12.claim: An may introduce either a verbal noun or an explanation of their whisper; the prohibition means not enabling the poor to enter.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p242/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p242/r13.speaker: عبد الله وابن أبي عبلة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p242/r13.claim: They read لا يدخلنها without أن, either supplying “they say” or treating whispering like speech.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p479#3/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p479#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p479#3/r1.claim: They whispered to one another not to let a poor person enter the garden that day.

ALUSI-FULL:v29p31#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p31#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p31#2/r1.claim: أن لا is explanatory of the speech implied by their whispering, or a verbal noun with omitted ب; a reading by Abdullah and Ibn Abi ʿAbla omits أن and supports the first parse.

ALUSI-FULL:v29p31#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p31#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p31#2/r2.claim: Some supply an implied قول, while the Kufan analysis makes يتخافتون govern the phrase because it contains the sense of speech.

ALUSI-FULL:v29p31#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p31#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p31#2/r3.claim: Telling the poor person not to enter dramatizes a broader order not to let one in, like saying لا أرينك ههنا.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p196/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p196/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p196/r1.claim: They set out whispering privately to one another that no poor person should enter the garden that day.

BAYDAWI-FULL:68:23-25/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:68:23-25/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:68:23-25/r2.claim: أن is explanatory, or is omitted in a reading with an implicit speech verb; telling the poor not to enter hyperbolically forbids allowing them entry.

BINTSHATI:v2p63/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p63/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p63/r3.claim: Takhāfut means whispering to one another so no one else hears the plan.

BINTSHATI:v2p63/r9.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p63/r9.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p63/r9.claim: Exegetes elaborate the garden story: it belonged to a righteous man who left it to his people and town; reports place it in Yemen near Ṣanʿāʾ, Abyssinia, or among the People of Scripture.

NAHHAS:v5p11/r2.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p11/r2.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p11/r2.claim: The answer is in an as before; ʿAbd Allāh's reading omits an because yatakhāfatūn means they speak secretly.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p105/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p105/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p105/r5.claim: The prohibition is phrased as barring a poor person from entering, but rhetorically they are forbidding themselves from letting one in; they intend to search throughout the day so none can reach fruit or an opening.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p82/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p82/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p82/r11.claim: The phrase forbidding any poor person to enter explains the whispering, since تخافت implies speech without stating its words.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p82/r12.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p82/r12.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p82/r12.claim: The emphatic ن in the prohibition reinforces their oath; grammatically the poor person is barred from entering, but the intended command is that no brother let one in.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p349#3/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p349#3/r5.speaker: ابن مسعود وابن أبي عبلة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p349#3/r5.claim: Ibn Masud and Ibn Abi Abla read لا يدخلنها without the particle أن.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p196/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p196/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p196/r3.claim: They spoke secretly so no one could hear their plan to prevent a poor person from entering the garden that day.

JISHUMI:v10p7036/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7036/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7036/r4.claim: The poor had an enforceable due in the harvest, variously identified as a tenth or as the fruit that fell during picking.

SAMIN-DURR:68:24/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:68:24/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:68:24/r1.claim: أن لا يدخلنها may be a verbal-noun clause reporting what they whispered or an explanatory clause after the speech-like verb.

SAMIN-DURR:68:24/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:68:24/r2.speaker: عبد الله وابن أبي عبلة
SAMIN-DURR:68:24/r2.claim: They read لا يدخلها without أن, either with an omitted القول under Basran analysis or by treating يتخافتون like a verb of speech under Kufan analysis.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p68/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p68/r10.speaker: يحيى بن سلام
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p68/r10.claim: They resolved that no poor person should enter the garden that day.

MUJAHID:v2p688/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p688/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v2p688/r1.claim: Mujahid says they privately resolved not to let any poor person enter the garden.

MUQATIL:68:17-27/r7.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:68:17-27/r7.speaker: author
MUQATIL:68:17-27/r7.claim: They decided to let no poor person enter the garden that day.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p270#4/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p270#4/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p270#4/r1.claim: The particle “an” may explain their whispering; if omitted, a verb of saying is understood. They prohibit enabling a poor person to enter, not merely his entering.

RAZI-FULL:v30p79/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p79/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p79/r1.claim: An is explanatory; Ibn Masʿūd reads without it, with an implicit verb of saying. Barring the poor from entering means the owners must not let them in.

STUDYQURAN:68:17/r8.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:68:17/r8.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:68:17/r8.claim: The brothers’ exclusion of the poor violated an ancient Near Eastern custom allowing the poor to glean and the Quranic command to give the harvest due on harvest day.

ASAD-NOTES:68:21#n13/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:68:21#n13/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:68:21#n13/r1.claim: Since Biblical times the poor have been understood to possess a right to a share of the harvest, as 6:141 states.

ASAD-NOTES:68:21#n13/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:68:21#n13/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:68:21#n13/r2.claim: The owners' resolve to deny the poor this right is the parable's second, specifically social, sin and connects with vv.10-13.

TAB-FULL:v23p171/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p171/r2.speaker: عكرمة
TAB-FULL:v23p171/r2.claim: ʿIkrima says the owners were Ethiopians whose father fed the poor from his garden; after he died, his sons called him foolish and vowed to exclude the poor.

TAB-FULL:v23p171/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p171/r3.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v23p171/r3.claim: Qatāda says the garden belonged to a charitable old man; his sons opposed his charity and, after his death, set out to keep poor people away.

TABATABAI:68:20-28/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:68:20-28/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:68:20-28/r5.claim: They went quietly, consulting in secret to keep poor people from noticing and claiming a share of the harvested fruit.

TABATABAI:68:1-33#5/r11.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:68:1-33#5/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
TABATABAI:68:1-33#5/r11.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas tells of a father who always gave each rightful person a share, then five sons who planned to keep an unusually abundant harvest from Muslim poor; four agreed and the moderate brother objected.

TABRISI:68:17-33/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:68:17-33/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:68:17-33/r8.claim: The command that no poor person should enter was the secret they exchanged.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:68:22-27/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:68:22-27/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:68:22-27/r3.claim: They conspire that no poor person should enter their orchard that day.

ELMALILI:68:7-33#5/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:7-33#5/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:68:7-33#5/r5.claim: They meant to finish the harvest completely and leave nothing for anyone, acting with extreme greed.

ELMALILI:68:7-33#5/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:7-33#5/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:68:7-33#5/r6.claim: They forgot that the previous day they had needed oaths to reassure each other and establish their company; the orchard's yield would likewise depend on trust.

ELMALILI:68:7-33#5/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:7-33#5/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:68:7-33#5/r7.claim: They should have remembered that God gave them the orchard and watched over it while they slept, and that God and needy servants had rights in it.

ELMALILI:68:7-33#5/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:7-33#5/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:68:7-33#5/r8.claim: Gratitude required generosity toward the poor, sharing some means from the crop, and cultivating beneficiaries and well-wishers instead of enemies through greed and despotism.

ELMALILI:68:7-33#5/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:7-33#5/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:68:7-33#5/r9.claim: They rushed out without considering the orchard's condition and whispered their exclusion of the poor so no one would hear.
